description: FiveFold is a diverse team of 5 students from different backgrounds, based in Malaysia. We are interested in coding, machine learning and artificial intelligence. After recent firsthand exposure to the ongoing haze situation in Malaysia, this challenge especially speaks to us as we wish to be able to contribute to the detection and suppression of wildfires.
summary:
EmberWatch is an interactive web application designed to monitor and analyze active fires and thermal anomalies across Southeast Asia. The platform addresses the challenge of fragmented satellite data by combining observations from NASA’s MODIS and VIIRS instruments into a single, unified dashboard.

The web app features an interactive GIS map with custom sensor layers, a daily burning activity calendar that tracks historical baseline departures, and analytics panels for comparing satellite resolutions. Behind the scenes, EmberWatch securely fetches data from NASA’s FIRMS API, runs a robust cleaning pipeline to quarantine errors and verify records, and standardizes different sensor resolutions onto common grid cells using a Harmonised Activity Index.

details:
EmberWatch pulls raw thermal anomaly feeds from NASA’s FIRMS API, verifying every download via SHA-256 checksums in SQLite to guarantee data integrity. Its backend cleaning engine normalizes timestamps, validates coordinates, and quarantines malformed entries transparently. To fix sensor resolution disparities, it maps MODIS (1 km) and VIIRS (375 m) data onto uniform spatial grids to compute a reliable Harmonised Activity Index (HAI).

The platform features an intuitive Streamlit dashboard housing an interactive Leaflet GIS map, a daily burning activity calendar tracking historical baseline departures, and Chart.js analytics. Our primary goal is to bridge the gap between complex raw satellite telemetry and actionable public intelligence, helping environmental researchers, policymakers, and local communities detect peatland fires early, track seasonal agricultural burning trends, and strengthen regional climate resilience across Southeast Asia.

The project is built using Python, Streamlit, SQLite, Tailwind CSS, Leaflet.js, and Chart.js. Key design choices focused on eliminating sensor bias, maintaining strict UTC auditability, and preventing silent data discards.
